Enterprise AI Adoption Statistics 2026

Explainerlowob research

By lowob · 16 November 2026 · 9-minute read · Strategy

Nearly nine in ten respondents to McKinsey's 2026 survey say their organisations regularly use AI in at least one function, but only 44% say AI is scaling across the enterprise, and the US Census Bureau puts current use at 17% to 20% of US businesses. Adoption rises steeply with company size and is concentrated in information and finance. Measured returns trail far behind use.

This page collects the enterprise AI adoption statistics most cited in 2026, each with its source, sample and date. It is the wider context for our hub piece, What Is an AI Agent?: agents are arriving inside companies whose general AI use is broad but often shallow. For agent-specific figures, see AI Agent Statistics 2026.

The figures disagree because they measure different populations. A survey of large-company executives and a government sample of all US employers will never give the same answer, and neither is wrong.

What percentage of companies use AI in 2026?

Anywhere from 19.8% to nearly nine in ten, depending on who is asked. The Census Bureau's sample of US employers gives 19.8% as of May 2026; McKinsey's sample of organisations already engaged with AI gives nearly nine in ten.

Ramp's figure sits between the two because it measures something different: a positive transaction for an AI product in a month. Ramp notes that free tools and employees' personal accounts do not show up, so its 56.8% likely understates use among its customers. Menlo's 65% comes from its survey of US enterprise AI decision-makers.

Does company size change AI adoption?

Yes, sharply in government data and less so in spending data. The Census Bureau found 37% of firms with 250 or more employees using AI against under 20% of firms with four or fewer.

McKinsey sees the same gradient in depth: 54% of respondents at $1 billion-plus organisations report enterprise-wide scaling, against one-third at smaller ones. Ramp's October 2026 data is the exception, with mid-market (66.7%) and SMB (63.2%) customers ahead of enterprise (59.0%). Ramp's sample is its own customers, so this is not a national picture.

Which industries use AI the most?

Information and finance lead. As of 3 May 2026 the Census Bureau put AI use at 39.7% in the information sector and 33.9% in finance and insurance, against 19.8% nationally and about 14% in retail trade. Use in the two leading sectors did not change significantly between December 2025 and May 2026.

How many employees use AI at work?

Fewer than company figures suggest. Pew's September 2025 survey found 21% of US workers doing at least some of their work with AI, while 65% said they do not use AI much or at all in their job.

Among large companies the shift in 2026 was rapid. KPMG's US leaders reported significant workforce adoption at 44% in Q3 2026, up from 10% a year earlier. Zapier's March 2026 survey found 94% of large US organisations using AI in some capacity, alongside 77% calling workforce AI skills an urgent need. Both are self-reports by executives, not usage logs.

Is enterprise AI adoption producing returns?

For a minority. McKinsey found 37% of respondents attributing any EBIT impact to AI in 2026, essentially unchanged from 2025, and about 6% qualifying as high performers. KPMG's global survey found only 12% consistently assessing AI value against cost.

What separates the high performers is not access to tools. McKinsey reports that nearly three-quarters of them have fundamentally redesigned workflows, against one-quarter of other respondents. Our guide How to Measure AI ROI sets out a method for a mid-size firm, and Which AI Assistant, Which Seats covers the first purchase decision.

lowob takeaways

  • Quote the population with the figure. 19.8% of US businesses and nearly nine in ten McKinsey respondents are both correct.
  • Size is the strongest predictor. Census data shows 37% of firms with 250+ employees using AI, against 19.8% nationally.
  • Use is broad, scale is not. 44% of McKinsey respondents report enterprise-wide scaling, and only 37% attribute any EBIT impact to AI.
  • Workflow redesign marks the leaders. High performers redesign how work is done, not only which tools are licensed.

Common questions

What percentage of companies use AI in 2026?

The US Census Bureau put current AI use at 19.8% of US businesses as of 3 May 2026. McKinsey's August 2026 survey found nearly nine in ten respondents' organisations regularly using AI in at least one function. Ramp found 56.8% of businesses on its platform paying for AI in October 2026. The gap reflects who was sampled, not a contradiction.

What percentage of large companies use AI?

The Census Bureau found 37% of US firms with 250 or more employees using AI in the period to May 2026. Among McKinsey's respondents, 54% of those at organisations with $1 billion or more in revenue reported enterprise-wide scaling of AI, against one-third at smaller organisations. Menlo Ventures reported enterprise adoption rising from 55% to 65%.

Which industries have the highest AI adoption?

In US government data, the information sector leads at 39.7% of businesses using AI as of 3 May 2026, followed by finance and insurance at 33.9%. The national rate was 19.8%, and retail trade was about 14%. These figures come from the Census Bureau's Business Trends and Outlook Survey.

Is AI adoption delivering ROI for companies?

For a minority so far. McKinsey's 2026 survey found 37% of respondents attributing any EBIT impact to AI, essentially unchanged from 2025, and about 6% qualifying as high performers with at least 5% of EBIT from AI. KPMG found only 12% of global leaders consistently assessing AI value against cost in Q3 2026.

Sources and notes

  • McKinsey, The state of AI in 2026, 25 August 2026. Consultancy survey of 1,719 respondents in 97 countries, 4 May to 8 June 2026; weighted by GDP; self-reported.
  • US Census Bureau, AI use among businesses (BTOS), revised 22 May 2026. Government survey of US employer businesses, data 14 December 2025 to 3 May 2026.
  • Ramp, AI Index, data through October 2026. Transaction data from 85,000+ US businesses on a fintech vendor's platform; excludes free tools and personal accounts.
  • Menlo Ventures, 2026: The State of Enterprise AI, 3 November 2026. Investor research; Morning Consult survey of nearly 400 US enterprise decision-makers; Menlo invests in AI companies.
  • Stanford HAI, AI Index 2026, economy chapter and economy overview, April 2026. Academic compilation; organisational adoption figures are McKinsey's 2025 data.
  • KPMG, Q3 2026 AI Pulse, 24 September 2026, and Q3 Global AI Pulse, 24 September 2026. Consultancy surveys of senior leaders; KPMG sells AI services.
  • Zapier, AI skills survey, via Business Wire, April 2026. Vendor survey of 542 US executives at firms with 1,000+ employees; ±4% margin.
  • Pew Research Center, About 1 in 5 US workers now use AI in their job, 6 October 2025. Nonpartisan survey of 5,010 US workers; the most recent Pew worker figure we found.
  • S&P Global Market Intelligence, Generative AI shows rapid growth but yields mixed results, 27 October 2025. 451 Research survey of 1,006 respondents, October to November 2024.
